Entities named from the Phase 2 BPA and the seven requirements, as nouns already in use here rather than tables to build. NINE, and the two most interesting results are things that turned out NOT to be entities.

ENTITIES, each with what identifies it:
  Folio        — the instance; identified by its harness.json declaration root. Top of the one-way chain.
  Board        — NEW, and the only genuinely new entity. Identified by a board id. Note that board ids ALREADY EXIST as the keys of BoardPositions.boards, so the id is in use before anything declares what it names: today a board is a key with no object behind it.
  BoardPosition— identified by (board, note). Declared, merged in #601.
  Note         — CarriedNote, identified by `id`. LandingSticky is a variant of it, not a second entity: same identifier space.
  Page         — identified by slug.
  ContentNode  — a block on a page. Identified by (page, node.id); ADDRESSED by its declared `label`. The two are different facts and that distinction is the whole of R3.
  Kind         — identified by the kind string; an open registry.
  TodoIndex    — the published projection, identified by its path + $schema. Derived in full.
  ZoomThreshold— R2 requires it be declared data. It is an entity ONLY if it has an owner; see the relations step, it is the open question.

NOT ENTITIES, by the technique's own test (step 2: "an entity with no identifier is an attribute of something else"):
  NoteAnchor — three states, no identifier of its own, cannot exist apart from the note that holds it. An attribute of Note. It looked like an entity because it has a discriminated union shape; shape is not identity.
  Avatar     — keyed by kind in schemas/avatars.ts and meaningless without it. If the kind disappears the glyph is about nothing, which is step 3's disappearance test. An attribute of Kind. This is already how the code stores it; the model now says why that was right.
  Badge, StickyPanel — renderings of one query (R6). Step 5: a derived fact is never stored, and the badge's count IS the cardinality of the panel's set. Modelling "Badge" as a thing is precisely how a badge acquires its own number and drifts from its panel.

ONE CORRECTION TO PHASE 4, load-bearing for R3. I wrote that R3 "is cheap — the generator has both halves before it composes them". That is true on the PAGE side (gen-docs-pages blockLabel reads the declared label while it holds page and node) and FALSE on the todo-index side: readTodoFiles gives only todo.targetLabel, so emitting target:{page,node,label} needs a reverse index label -> (page,node) built from the page walk. Still cheap — the walk already happens in the same script — but it is a DERIVED JOIN, not two fields lying around. Modelling it makes the requirement honest: label is ContentNode's addressable name, and the pair is recovered by lookup, never by parsing the string, which is the burden R3 exists to remove.

Relations with cardinality stated in BOTH directions, per step 4 of the technique. Where the answer is "many" the ORDER is named or its absence is admitted. Four are answered from committed code or a recorded ruling; four are genuinely open and go to the confirmation lanes rather than being guessed — a wrong cardinality is invisible until the data arrives.

ANSWERED, with the evidence:
  Folio 1 --- 0..n Board        | a board belongs to exactly one folio. Order: by board id (the document's keys sort).
  Board 1 --- 0..n BoardPosition| a position belongs to exactly one board. Order: sortPositions, deterministic, and it is load-bearing for merging.
  BoardPosition n --- 1 Note    | a position names exactly one note. A NOTE MAY HAVE 0..n POSITIONS, one per board — stated outright in board-positions.ts ("One note may sit on several boards"). The arrow points down only: folio -> board -> position -> note, never back.
  Page 1 --- 0..n ContentNode   | a node belongs to exactly one page. Order: DOCUMENT ORDER, which R4 then depends on — the linear collapse IS this order.
  ContentNode n --- 1 Kind, Kind 1 --- 1 Avatar | with GENERIC as the total fallback, so the relation is total rather than partial-and-blank.
  ContentNode 1 --- 0..n Note   | the badge query, and R6 says the badge count IS this cardinality. Already true in mountPageStickies; unguarded.

OPEN — and each is open for a different reason:

1. Note --- ContentNode, the note's side. Today: 0..1, because NoteAnchor holds one block label. The ask says "be attached to nothing or show attachment to content nodeS based on relationships", plural. If a note may attach to several nodes, NoteAnchor's block state becomes a list and every consumer of targetLabel changes shape; if it stays one, "relationships" means the OTHER edges (tags.references, todoRelations) rendered as lines, which costs nothing new. Those are different features wearing one sentence.

2. Note --- Board, within one board. schemas/board-positions.ts stores an ARRAY per board, so the type admits a note twice; place() filters by note before concat, so the CODE enforces one. One fact, two answers, nothing asserting they agree — the exact shape data-modelling's own examples (sym3, 85e8) were made of. Either the type is wrong or place() is.

3. Board --- ContentNode. R1 says the board renders content; nothing says WHICH content. Three candidates with different data: everything in the folio (a board is a view, holds no selection), an explicit selection (a board is a document, and the new content type has a body), or derived from the notes placed on it (no new field, but an empty board can never show content).

4. ZoomThreshold's owner. R2 requires it be declared, not a literal — it does not say WHOSE property it is. Folio-wide (one number, one place, no per-kind legibility), per-kind (a dense table flips earlier than a title; Kind is already the avatar's owner so it is the natural home), or per-board (a board is a canvas and its author chose the scale). Step 3's disappearance test does not settle it: the number survives any single board and any single kind, which is an argument for the folio, but "when does THIS become unreadable" is plainly a fact about the thing being read.

WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS MODEL, written before the answers arrive so they cannot be fitted to it:
  - if Note ever needs x/y to answer a question, the position layer is in the wrong place and the owner's "on top of notes" ruling is wrong;
  - if two boards ever need to disagree about a note's ATTACHMENT (not its position), attachment belongs on the board and not on the note;
  - if the badge ever needs a number not equal to the panel's length, R6 is wrong rather than the implementation;
  - if a consumer must parse a string to answer "which page", R3 has not landed however many fields were added.

Entities confirmed by litlfred, acting as BA / feature requestor. The confirmation is INDIRECT and is recorded as such rather than upgraded: no entity was disputed, and all four answers were given in the model's own vocabulary (note, board, content node, kind, folio), which is the recognition this lane asks for — "are these the things?" is a naming question, and the names were used rather than corrected.

What was NOT separately asserted: nobody said "Board is the right name" in those words. If a name is wrong the loop returns here, which is cheap; the gateway loops back to A_Entities by design.

Three of the four answers ADD a fact, and each lands on a different entity — which is itself a check on the model, because a fact with no entity to sit on would have been the finding this phase exists to produce:
  Q1 -> Note gains a declared SECONDARY reference list (primary attachment unchanged).
  Q3 -> Board gains an OPTIONAL filter (absent = the whole folio).
  Q4 -> Folio gains a DEFAULT zoom threshold; Kind may override it.
Every one had a home. No requirement turned out to be about something nobody had named.

All four open cardinalities answered by litlfred, the only HUMAN stakeholder of the five recorded at A_Stakeholders. Answers verbatim as selected, each with what it settles and what it now costs:

Q1 -> "One primary + declared secondaries". Note --- ContentNode is 1:0..1 for the PRIMARY attachment (unchanged, so targetLabel, note-anchor and mountPageStickies keep working untouched), plus an explicit list of SECONDARY references. The badge counts PRIMARIES ONLY, which keeps R6 intact: the badge is still the cardinality of the panel's query, and the panel is still "notes whose primary attachment is here". Cost: one new field and one rule a consumer must know, and that rule must be EMITTED rather than documented or it is exactly the burden R3 exists to remove.

Q2 -> "One per board, make it structural". BoardPositions.boards moves from an ARRAY of {note,x,y} to a RECORD keyed by note id. The type then enforces what place() already enforced in code, so the two answers become one. Mergeability is preserved or improved: keys sort, each note occupies its own lines, which is the whole reason the document is indented. sortPositions, renderPositions, orphanPositions, place and unplace all change shape, and the 17 tests in board-positions.test.ts move with them. Merged only yesterday in PR #601 and nothing downstream consumes it yet, so the migration cost is a schema and its tests.

Q3 -> "Everything by default, optional declared filter". Board --- ContentNode is 0..n and DERIVED: absent filter means the whole folio, so nothing can go stale and content added later appears by itself. A board MAY narrow. The filter is a declared query, not a stored list — the difference is that a list needs a staleness check and a query does not.

Q4 -> "Folio default, a kind may override". ZoomThreshold is NOT an entity: it is a fact on Folio with an override on Kind, which is the repository's own inheritance rule (inherit everything, override anything; a variant states only what it CHANGES). Requiredness is checked AFTER resolution — a kind that states nothing is complete, not invalid. An override CITES WHY, per the same skill, so the model records where the value came from and not only what it is.

WHAT THIS SETTLES ABOUT THE ASK ITSELF: Q1's answer means "show attachment to content nodes based on relationships" is ONE feature, not two — a primary attachment that behaves as today, and secondary references drawn as lines. That was the sentence carrying two features, and it now carries one.

Entities recognised and every cardinality answered — the two conditions this gateway names, both met in the same exchange. Four questions asked with selectable options, four answered; none deferred, so the loop leaves rather than returning to A_Entities. The skill's own exit rule is the reason the count matters: a model with one unanswered cardinality is not 95 per cent done, it is a model with a hole exactly where the exceptions live.

The model is DECLARED, with a reader shipped in the same change — step 6 of the technique, and the part it insists on: "a field with no consumer is not a model, it is a comment with punctuation."

WHAT LANDED, one module per answered question:
  Q2 -> schemas/board-positions.ts reshaped. boards[board] moves from an ARRAY of {note,x,y} to a RECORD keyed by note id, so "two positions for one note" is UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely unreachable through place(). New readers positionsOn() and positionOf() convert the map to a list at the one place that should: a map is the right storage because it makes a duplicate impossible, a list is the right thing to render. 25 tests, including one asserting the OLD array document no longer validates.
  Q3 -> schemas/board.ts, NEW. The Board entity the positions layer has been keying by since it merged, with nothing behind it. Optional filter, two axes (pages, kinds), OR within an axis and AND across them, absent means the whole folio. Readers boardShows() and boardContent(); document order preserved because R4's linear collapse renders that order. 17 tests.
  Q4 -> schemas/semantic-zoom.ts, NEW. Folio default with a per-kind override; `because` REQUIRED on every override and zoomThresholdFor() returns the SOURCE alongside the value, because an inherited value is still a fact somebody must be able to trace. 14 tests.
  Q1 -> schemas/note-anchor.ts gains AlsoAboutSchema, alsoAboutLabels(), notesAt() and badgeAt(); carried-note.ts gains the optional `alsoAbout` field. notesAt returns BOTH relations from one pass so a badge and its panel cannot be built apart, which is R6 made structural rather than documented. badgeAt carries R5's >1 threshold with the exact count kept for aria-label. 7 tests added.

THE LAYERING IS ASSERTED, NOT ASSUMED. board.ts and board-positions.ts each have a test reading their own source and requiring their import list to be exactly ["zod"]. The owner's "notes exist lower down than folio, make sure arrows correct" is a property a future edit can break silently, so it is checked at the import level rather than described.

WHAT IS NOT DECLARED HERE, deliberately: no instance, no folio wiring, no renderer. A_Declare asks for a model a tool can read; the board a folio actually owns, the harness.json wiring for the zoom document and the rendering are implementation units for Phase 5's beans. The schemas are the contract they will be built against.

CHECK BEFORE CREATE was run rather than asserted. 523 beans scanned against board|miro|avatar|zoom|tile|fsh-guts|sticky|panel|visualis|xss; 30 matched and five are live neighbours that these beans REFERENCE instead of duplicating: 1le7 already owns the tile template (zsah says extend it, never mint a second), 7vhe owns the fsh-guts viewer and counter, d1r6 already discards a sticky to fsh-guts and db7g generalises that ONE path rather than growing a second, 4kj4 owns per-kind avatars, and xgd8/jbx2/v1hw own the visualisers a tile opens. beans create dedupes on nothing, so an unguarded re-run is how a repo once produced 14,688 duplicates.

ONE STRUCTURAL CHANGE, FLAGGED RATHER THAN QUIET. check:bean-parents enforces milestone -> epic -> feature -> task and a FEATURE MAY NOT BE A PARENT AT ALL, so ten tasks under feature 6lb8 failed two gates. 6lb8 is now an EPIC, and because an epic's parent must be a milestone rather than another epic, its parent moved from yj32 (epic) to p5wm (GOAL 2, milestone). Nothing about the work changed and nothing was lost — yj32's own parent IS p5wm, so this sits in the same goal one level up. The alternative, reparenting the ten tasks onto yj32 directly, is equally one line of front matter and the owner can have it instead. Recorded in 6lb8's body too, because a tree that moved silently is a tree nobody can trust.

WHAT THE BEANS COVER THAT THE REQUIREMENTS DID NOT. R8-R17 arrived AFTER GW_Reqs closed, in two messages. They are additive — checked against the declared model rather than assumed, and nothing already built is invalidated — but they are a second requirements round and the beans are written against both rounds. Sign-off says so explicitly rather than presenting eleven beans as though one requirements set produced them.
